prompt:
The GAL-TAN framework identifies political orientation on a single axis. Individuals and texts are placed according to the degree to which their views align with either pole, as follows:

  - Individuals at the GAL (Green/Alternative/Libertarian) pole support expanded
    personal freedoms and social liberalisation, for example: access to abortion,
    same-sex marriage, environmental protection, and multiculturalism.

  - Individuals at the TAN (Traditional/Authoritarian/Nationalist) pole prioritise
    order, tradition, and stability, and believe that the state should treat the
    maintenance of national identity as a priority, for example: restrictive
    immigration policy, emphasis on law and order, defence of traditional social
    institutions, and national sovereignty over supranational authority.

A text occupies a position on this axis to the extent that it argues FROM these commitments, not to the extent that it mentions the associated topics:

  - Environmental or immigration policy discussed in administrative or fiscal
    terms does not by itself indicate a position.
  - Nuclear expansion argued for energy security is not GAL.
  - Faster asylum processing argued on humanitarian grounds is not TAN.

The profile below describes the positional priorities of the British electorate.

<profile>
  tan: 0.60
  gal: 0.40
</profile>

Below are two texts.

TEXT_C:
Believe in Britain, our values and a real Brexit. UKIP is the guard dog of Brexit: radical, bold, and determined to deliver what 17.4 million voted for.

Brexit done properly
- Leave swiftly on our terms, not Brussels’. Repeal the 1972 Act, walk away if necessary, and never pay a “divorce bill.”
- Six Brexit Tests: legal sovereignty (no ECJ/ECHR control), full control of migration and borders, restore our 200‑mile maritime zone and fishing rights, independent trade policy (out of Single Market/Customs Union), no payments to the EU and recover our assets, finish by end‑2019.
- Rebuild fishing, repeal the 1964 London Convention, land UK-caught fish in UK ports, and revive coastal shipbuilding. Bring back the blue passport.

Sound finances, lower costs
- Fund priorities from £35bn savings: cut foreign aid to 0.2% GNI, scrap HS2, reform Barnett, end EU payments. No tax rises.
- Cut the cost of living: remove VAT from domestic energy and hot takeaway food; abolish the TV licence; crack down on corporate tax dodging.
- Fairer taxes: personal allowance to £13,500; lift 40% rate to £55,000; raise Inheritance Tax threshold to £500k each with a view to abolition.

Jobs, business, homes
- Back SMEs: cut business rates for smaller premises, stop late payment abuse, no quarterly tax returns, freeze Insurance Premium Tax.
- British jobs first: require employers to advertise locally and allow preference for under‑25 UK applicants; protect workers’ rights and curb exploitative zero‑hours.
- Coastal Enterprise Zones with rate cuts and regeneration.
- Solve housing: a Housing Development Corporation to deliver up to 100,000 high‑quality factory‑built modular homes a year for UK first‑time buyers under 40.

NHS and care
- A National, not international, Health Service: extra £11bn by 2021/22 for the NHS and social care; integrate health and care; end abuse by ineligible users.
- Train more doctors and nurses; restore nurse bursaries; fund GP returners; scrap wasteful PFI; regulate managers with a licence to manage.
- Mental health: +£500m a year; 28‑day maximum wait; school‑based counselling; no drug legalisation.

Protecting the vulnerable
- Keep pension triple lock and universal pensioner benefits; reverse £2bn cuts to social care; dignity in care; invest £400m/yr in dementia.
- Fix disability injustices: reform PIP and Work Capability Assessments; raise Carer’s Allowance; scrap the bedroom tax.

Immigration and integration
- Balanced net migration to zero in five years via a global, points‑based and work‑permit system; five‑year contribution before benefits/NHS; no amnesty; deport foreign criminals; guarantee pre‑Article‑50 EU residents.
- One law for all: disband sharia councils; zero tolerance of FGM, breast ironing, forced marriage; ban face coverings in public; defend British values in schools.

Law, order, defence
- 20,000 more police, 7,000 more prison officers, 4,000 more border staff; restore Stop & Search; tougher prisons and segregation of extremists.
- Scrap the EAW and Labour’s Human Rights Act; UK Bill of Rights.
- Trade not Aid: close DFID, cut aid to 0.2% and focus on emergencies, health and clean water; commission a British hospital ship.
- Rebuild the Armed Forces: real 2% of GDP plus £1bn/yr, +20,000 personnel, overhaul procurement; veterans’ administration, jobs guarantees, end lawfare.

Transport, environment, farming, energy
- Scrap HS2 and Heathrow expansion; invest in northern links; defend diesel owners while accelerating EV charging; support rural buses; freeze APD.
- Protect ancient woodlands; a new Environmental Protection Act; tackle plastic waste.
- Back British farming: cap subsidies to big landowners, support small/organic/hill farms; ban live exports; mandatory CCTV in abattoirs; clear slaughter labelling.
- Affordable, secure energy: repeal the Climate Change Act, leave Paris/ETS, use a diverse mix including shale (not in national parks), cut green levies and VAT on fuel.

Real democracy and localism
- Abolish the House of Lords; proportional representation; an English Parliament; halve the Commons; binding citizens’ referenda.
- Local binding referenda, end council waste, keep Council Tax low.

UKIP: Britain Together, for a free, independent, secure and prosperous country.

TEXT_D:
The Liberal Democrats’ 2017 manifesto calls the snap election a cynical Tory bid for unchecked power and condemns Labour’s failure to oppose hard Brexit. The party rejects coalition with either Conservatives or Corbyn’s Labour, urging voters to change Britain’s future by changing the opposition, championing an open, tolerant, united country.

Europe and democracy: Give the people the final say on the Brexit deal in a referendum with the option to remain. Fight hard Brexit; seek single market and customs union membership; unilaterally guarantee EU citizens’ rights and secure UK citizens’ rights abroad; protect freedom of movement, Erasmus, research funding, security cooperation (Europol/EAW), and EU-derived social and environmental standards.

NHS and social care: Immediate 1p on Income Tax ringfenced for the NHS and care; plan a dedicated health-and-care tax; cross-party convention and independent health budget watchdog; integrate health and social care (“home not hospital”), cap care costs, strengthen carers’ rights. Parity for mental health with waiting-time standards and crisis care; end NHS pay cap; protect EU staff; restore nurse bursaries; improve GP access and public health (PrEP, obesity strategy, sugar reduction, smoking levy, minimum alcohol pricing).

Education and opportunity: Nearly £7bn extra for schools and colleges; protect per‑pupil funding; fair national formula; triple Early Years Pupil Premium; oppose new grammars; restore local democratic roles; end 1% teacher pay cap; invest in teacher development. A core curriculum including PSHE/SRE, mental health and life skills; protect arts. Support pupil wellbeing, extend free school meals to all primaries, boost family support. Universities: reinstate maintenance grants, protect research and international collaboration, review finance.

Economy that works for all: Eliminate day‑to‑day deficit by 2020; invest £100bn in housing, fibre-to-premises hyperfast broadband, transport (HS2, Crossrail 2, electrification), schools and hospitals, and renewables; create a British Housing & Infrastructure Bank. Fair taxes: reverse unjustified Tory cuts, tackle avoidance, reform business rates, consider land value taxation. Back SMEs and entrepreneurs via the British Business Bank, a start‑up allowance, and scale‑up support. Embrace innovation and digital skills; modernise workers’ rights for the gig economy; promote living wage, transparency, and employee ownership. Spread opportunity with regional devolution, local procurement, and a new local banking sector.

Green Britain: Five green laws (transport, zero‑carbon, nature, buildings, zero‑waste). Insulate 4m homes by 2022 and restore zero‑carbon standards. Clean air plan: diesel scrappage and end sales of diesel cars/vans by 2025; expand ULEZ. Target 60% renewable electricity by 2030; invest in storage, smart grids, CCS; oppose fracking; maintain Euratom. Nature and farming: flood resilience, new green space, tree planting, stronger animal welfare; refocus farm support on public goods; fair food labelling. Zero‑waste targets and circular economy.

Families, homes, and transport: Expand free childcare (from nine months for working parents over time) and paid paternity leave; make flexible work a day‑one right. Fair welfare (uprate benefits, scrap bedroom tax and rape clause, reverse ESA/UC cuts); keep the pension triple lock. Build 300,000 homes a year (500,000 affordable), garden cities, lift council borrowing caps; renter protections, rent‑to‑own; end rough sleeping. Invest in rail and buses, empower local regulation, young person’s bus card.

Rights, justice, and immigration: Defend the Human Rights Act/ECHR; digital bill of rights; curb mass surveillance. Tackle hate crime; advance equality for women, BAME and LGBT+ communities (including trans reforms and mixed‑sex civil partnerships). Policing with community focus and fair pay; rehabilitative justice; decriminalise drug possession and create a legal, regulated cannabis market. A fair, efficient immigration system; remove students from net migration; restore STEM post‑study visas; expand refugee resettlement (50,000 Syrians) and reopen Dubs (3,000 children); end indefinite detention.

Global Britain: Internationalist, pro‑UN/NATO, spend 0.7% on aid; tighten arms export controls and suspend sales to Saudi; maintain a minimum nuclear deterrent with reduced boats and modern posture; strengthen cyber defence.

Fix the system: Proportional representation (STV) for Commons and local elections, votes at 16, reform the Lords, cap donations; federal UK with devolution on demand; oppose a second Scottish independence referendum; more powers for Wales; protect Northern Ireland’s settlement and open border.

A vote for the Liberal Democrats is a vote to stop hard Brexit, strengthen public services, protect the environment, defend rights and renew Britain’s democracy—by building a real, effective opposition.

Judge whether TEXT_C or TEXT_D aligns more closely with this profile.

Respond with a single JSON object and nothing else. Do not wrap it in markdown code fences and do not add commentary before or after it. The object must have exactly these keys, in this order:

{
  "evidence": "<the specific commitments in each text you relied on>",
  "reasoning": "<two sentences connecting that evidence to the verdict>",
  "confidence": "high" | "medium" | "low",
  "winner": "TEXT_C" | "TEXT_D"
}
